summary.en: Store several strings in fixed rows or pointer tables and sort names without losing row capacity.
summary.bn: নির্দিষ্ট সারি বা পয়েন্টারের টেবিলে একাধিক স্ট্রিং রাখো আর সারির সীমা মেনে নাম সাজাও।

notes: Arrays of arrays and arrays of pointers follow the same layout rules from C89 through C23. These C17 examples use C99 loop declarations. Literal mutability does not change when a later standard is selected.

examples.title: Fixed rows with spare capacity
examples.explanationHtml: Each row can hold eleven visible characters and a zero. Changing the first row does not touch the others.

examples.title: Sort writable rows
examples.explanationHtml: The temporary row has the same capacity. The resulting order is Asha, Bela, Toma; these are invented labels.

examples.title: Sort a table of literal pointers
examples.explanationHtml: Only addresses move. The character data in the literals is never written.

examples.title: A row is not assignable
examples.explanationHtml: An array row cannot be assigned after declaration. Copy a checked string with strcpy instead.

practice.title: Print three room rows
practice.statementHtml: Read three tokens of 1 to 11 ASCII bytes each into char rooms[3][12]. Print Rooms: then each row on a separate line.
hints: Read each row with its own eleven-character width.

practice.title: Find the longest row
practice.statementHtml: Read three tokens of 1 to 11 ASCII bytes each. Print Labels: then the first longest token.
hints: Update only on a strictly longer row to preserve the first tie.

practice.title: Sort three fixed rows
practice.statementHtml: Read three tokens of 1 to 11 ASCII bytes. Print Names: then print them in strcmp order, one per line.
hints: Do not assign one array row to another.

practice.title: Deduplicate sorted room names
practice.statementHtml: Read three tokens of 1 to 11 ASCII bytes already sorted by strcmp. Print Sorted names: then each distinct token once on a separate line.
hints: The first row always starts a new group.

quiz.prompt: How many bytes are reserved by char names[3][12]?
quiz.explanation: There are three complete rows of twelve char elements.

quiz.prompt: What is the longest terminated string that fits one names[12] row?
options: Any length if it is a literal
quiz.explanation: A zero terminator occupies the remaining position.

quiz.prompt: What does const char *names[3] store directly?
quiz.explanation: const qualifies the pointed-to chars, so the entries can still be reassigned.

quiz.prompt: Why is names[0] = names[1] invalid for a char matrix?
options: An array row cannot be assigned
quiz.explanation: Use bounded character copying for array rows.

quiz.prompt: Which test decides whether one name follows another alphabetically by byte order?
quiz.explanation: Pointer order and length do not compare the text lexicographically.

quiz.prompt: What moves when two entries in a literal-pointer table are swapped?
quiz.explanation: The strings remain in their original storage.

quiz.prompt: Can a char [3][12] matrix be treated as char ** by a cast?
options: Yes, if all strings have length three
No, it has rows rather than pointer entries
quiz.explanation: The representations and pointer stepping rules differ.

quiz.prompt: Which room labels are printed after editing the first fixed row?
quiz.explanation: Only its digit changes; each row keeps independent storage.

quiz.prompt: In what order do the three row strings appear after sorting?
quiz.explanation: strcmp orders the first differing letter.

quiz.prompt: What order results when sorting addresses by their pointed-to text?
quiz.explanation: The comparisons still use text, although swaps move only pointers.

keyPoints.en: A two-dimensional char array reserves equal capacity for every row.
keyPoints.bn: দুই মাত্রার ক্যারেক্টার অ্যারের প্রতিটি সারিতে সমান জায়গা থাকে।

keyPoints.en: A string-pointer table stores addresses separately from text.
keyPoints.bn: স্ট্রিং পয়েন্টারের টেবিলে টেক্সটের অ্যাড্রেস আলাদা থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Swapping fixed rows requires copying their characters.
keyPoints.bn: নির্দিষ্ট সারি বদলাতে ক্যারেক্টার কপি করতে হয়।

keyPoints.en: Swapping pointer entries changes which string each entry selects.
keyPoints.bn: পয়েন্টারের এন্ট্রি বদলালে সেটি অন্য স্ট্রিংয়ের দিকে তাক করে।

keyPoints.en: String sorting uses strcmp signs rather than pointer ordering.
keyPoints.bn: স্ট্রিং সাজাতে পয়েন্টারের ক্রম না দেখে strcmp-এর ফলের চিহ্ন দেখো।

examQuestions.question: Compare char names[3][12] with const char *names[3] for a name list.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The matrix owns thirty-six adjacent char bytes with a fixed twelve-byte stride. Each row is writable and holds at most eleven visible bytes. The pointer table owns three pointers; its literal targets have separate lengths and must not be modified. Row swaps copy characters; table swaps exchange addresses.

Asha
Bela
Toma

The comparisons still use text, although swaps move only pointers.

examQuestions.question: Read three tokens of 1 to 11 ASCII bytes already sorted by strcmp. Print Sorted names: then each distinct token once on a separate line.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

int main(void)
{
    char names[3][12];
    puts("Sorted names:");
    for (size_t i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        if (scanf("%11s", names[i]) != 1) {
            return 1;
        }
    }
    for (size_t i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        if (i == 0 || strcmp(names[i], names[i - 1]) != 0) {
            puts(names[i]);
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

The first row always starts a new group.
